newsitem.title: USA: Rain relieves dry Florida citrus groves.
newsitem.headline: Rain relieves dry Florida citrus groves.

text.p: Florida's citrus groves received much-welcome rain late last week after sufferring weeks of hot and dry conditions, said Florida Agricultural Statistics Service (FASS).
Rainfall ranged from just spotty showers to about two inches in some areas. Temperatures for the week ended March 16 ranged from the low 50s (degrees Fahrenheit) to the 80s.

Many growers had been irrigating crops to maintain good tree condition during the bloom period. Trees of all varieties have reached full open bloom while others have only swelling buds with few open flowers, FASS said.
Harvest of mid-season and early-season oranges is nearly complete as the Valencia harvest gets underway, FASS said.
FASS said an estimated 2,295,000 boxes of Valencia oranges were harvested in the week ended March 16, up from 1,474,000 in the prior week and compared with 1,924,000 during the week ended March 2.
About 1,000 boxes of navel oranges were harvested in the week ended March 16, down from 5,000 boxes the previous week and 29,000 boxes in the week ended March 2.
An estimated 844,000 boxes of early and mid oranges were harvested in the week ended March 16, down from 2,157,000 boxes the prior week, FASS said.
